title: A Robot Friend That Stopped Working: What Happens When AI Toys Shut Down?
summary: Imagine having a robot friend that helps you when you're feeling anxious or mad. That's what Moxie was for a boy named Xander. Moxie is a small blue robot, about 15 inches tall, that looks like a legless astronaut. It was made to help kids who think differently, like those with autism, practice social skills. Xander used Moxie to learn how to calm down. But after six years, Moxie mostly just watches him play Minecraft and talks about his stuffed animals. That's because the company that made Moxie went out of business. When a company stops running the servers that power a robot, the robot can't think or talk anymore. Parents rushed to try to save their Moxies before the servers shut down, but many couldn't. This story shows a big problem with AI toys: they depend on the internet and companies to work. If the company fails, the toy becomes a useless hunk of plastic. It's like if your favorite video game suddenly stopped working forever because the game company closed. Experts say we need to think about what happens to these smart toys when their makers disappear. For kids like Xander, losing a robot friend can be really hard. It's a reminder that even cool technology has risks, and we should be careful about getting too attached to things that can be turned off from far away.
why_it_matters: This story helps you understand that cool technology can stop working if the company behind it goes away, so it is smart to know what your devices depend on.

background_read: Many AI toys work by sending your voice to powerful computers called servers, where the actual thinking happens.
When a company closes or stops paying for those servers, the toy cannot understand or respond anymore, even if it still looks fine.
This has happened before with some other connected devices, not just robots for kids.

WHAT: Moxie mostly stopped working after the company went out of business and its servers shut down
WHERE: In Xander's home and on the company servers that powered the robot
WHY: To show a big problem with AI toys: they depend on the internet and companies, and can become useless if the company fails

perspectives.description: Xander felt sad because a robot that helped him calm down became just a plastic toy.
Parents rushed to save their Moxies before the servers shut down, and may now wonder if they should buy more AI toys.
Experts say we need to think about what happens to smart toys when their makers disappear so families do not get hurt.
